own_solution.law: Circular Couette flow between coaxial cylinders (inner rotating, outer fixed, no-slip): torque T = 4 pi mu L Omega R1^2 R2^2/(R2^2 - R1^2); power P = T Omega.
assumptions: exact annular solution rather than the thin-gap approximation

T2F2B.regime: Taylor vortices would alter the torque only above the stated onset; 120 rpm << 6500 rpm.

TF18F.regime: Laminar Couette result holds below 6500 rpm; 120 rpm is inside.

notes: Omega = 4 pi = 12.566 rad/s; R1^2 R2^2/(R2^2-R1^2) = 1.936e-7/8.4e-5 = 2.3048e-3 m^2; 4 pi mu L = 0.50265; P = 0.50265 * 157.914 * 2.3048e-3 = 0.18294 W. At 195 rpm: 0.18294 * (195/120)^2 = 0.48309 W. A thin-gap (planar Couette) approximation would give 0.159 W, about 13% lower; the exact annular solution is the one implied by the stated laminar, steady, end-free flow. Density: it enters only the radial pressure balance of steady azimuthal flow, not the shear stress, so it drops out of the torque (C; it would matter only for stability, which the laminar statement fixes, so K would also be defensible). T4956 and TFDA3 carry no number.
